note: Ližnjan came third of eighteen towns in the rebuilt record sweep, behind only Rijeka and Svetvinčenat, and this archive had never given it a page. It got one because of a pin on a map — a line David had drawn years ago from Ližnjan to Monheim in Bavaria, with a note beside it reading «Grga dies in Zagreb», and no source of any kind.
lead: Grga turns out to be real, and the register holds two generations of his family.

grga.heading: Grga — Gregorius Defranceski of Ližnjan, born 1851

rows.lab: His marriage, and his age in it
rows.text: A marriage at Ližnjan on **10 June 1874**. The principal is **Gregorius Defranceski**, and the clerk records his age: **22**, which puts his birth in 1851. The record is filed under Croatia-Slavonia, Magyarország — the Hungarian half of the Monarchy — with the place tagged Ližnjan, Istria.

rows.lab: Who he married
rows.text: **Maria Vojnić.** She is named as the mother in every one of his children's baptisms. Vojnić is one of the great Ližnjan surnames — and it is one of the names standing beside «Defrančeski Ante» in the «Pučki prijatelj» subscription list of 27 February 1920.

rows.lab: His parents
rows.text: **Gregorio Defranceschi and Agata Skifić**, who appear across the Ližnjan books from the 1840s. The indexer has repeatedly merged the two surnames into «Gregorii Skifić» and «Agathæ Skifić», which is how a machine reads a Latin entry giving a father, a mother and her maiden name in one line. Read against the Italian-language entries of the same couple — «Gregorio Defranceschi» and «Agata Schiffich» — the household is unmistakable.

rows.lab: His children, from the baptism book
rows.text: **Anastasia**, baptised 23 February 1875 and again a child of the same name on 23 February 1876 — the second almost certainly named for the first. **Maria**, born 4 January 1878, baptised the 5th. **Justina**, born 3 October 1879, baptised the 4th. **Maria** again, born 25 January 1882, baptised the 26th — so the 1878 Maria had died. And **Josephus**, March 1887. Six baptisms in thirteen years and at least two of them replacing a dead child, which is the ordinary arithmetic of an Istrian village.

rows.lab: And where his daughters went
rows.text: **Justina Defrančeski** — spelt there with the háček — married **Josephus Fedel** at Ližnjan on 22 November 1898. **Stana Defranceski** married **Jacobus Vojnić** on 7 August 1899. Two Ližnjan houses, in two years.

rows.lab: The generation before him
rows.text: Gregorio and Agata's own children run back to the 1840s: Maria, 8 December 1846; Cattarina, 31 October 1847; a Giovanni; Agatha, born 30 December 1867 and baptised on New Year's Day 1868; a Maria who married Josephus Ruman on 17 November 1869; and a Lucia who married Joannes Sandalj on 11 February 1874, four months before her brother's wedding. Behind them stands a **Mattio De Franceschi** with a wife **Madalena Peucovich**, given as Gregorio's own parents.

rows.lab: A death that may be his sister's
rows.text: At Ližnjan on 6 October 1879, a **Lucia** died aged twenty-five, born 1854, buried the next day. The indexer could not tell from the page whether her husband was «Joannis Sandalj» or «Gregorii Defranceski» and wrote both. If she is the Lucia Defranceschi who married Joannes Sandalj in February 1874, then Grga buried his sister five years into her marriage and three days after his daughter Justina was baptised.

grga.source_g: FamilySearch record indexes for Ližnjan, Istria — 127 entries of this surname recovered in a targeted sweep, September 2026, spanning 1788 to the twentieth century. The marriage of 10 June 1874 is ark 1:1:XQM3-BLWJ; the baptism of 26 January 1882 is 1:1:XQM3-B4YH; the burial of 7 October 1879 is 1:1:XQM3-G3KW. Index entries, not images: the parish books themselves are at Pazin and have not been read.

monheim.heading: Monheim and Zagreb — corrected the same evening, by David's own tree

rows.lab: What the live tree gives
rows.text: Two Gregorios at Ližnjan, either side of the one found here. **Gregorio de Franceschi, born 23 May 1822 at Ližnjan, died there 25 November 1861** — old enough to be the father of the Gregorius who married in 1874 at twenty-two. And **Gregorius «Grgo» Defranceski, born 1931 at Ližnjan, died at Zagreb** — the man on the pin. Four generations of the name in one village, and the family knew about the last of them all along.

rows.lab: What the map says
rows.text: A line drawn from Ližnjan to **Monheim**, and a separate pin, «Petar Moves to Metzingen». The coordinates on the Monheim pin are 10.8537 E, 48.8427 N — which is **Monheim in Bavaria**, in the Donau-Ries, not Monheim am Rhein. It matters: Bavarian Monheim is about a hundred kilometres from Metzingen, and Metzingen is four kilometres from Pfullingen, where this family's own wartime papers were issued.

rows.lab: And what carries no source at all
rows.text: Nothing. The pin has no note, no date, no name and no document behind it, and neither does «Grga dies in Zagreb». They are David's own knowledge, drawn on a map some years ago. This archive has searched for both and found neither: no Defranceschi at Monheim in any index reachable from here, and no death for a Grga at Zagreb in the newspapers or the burial indexes.

rows.lab: And then David's own tree answered it, and this archive had the wrong man
rows.text: Read directly out of the live MyHeritage tree the same evening: **«Gregorius ‘Grgo’ Defranceski, born 1931 at Ližnjan, died at Zagreb.»** That is the Grga of the map pin, and he is not the Gregorius born in 1851 whom this page had just reconstructed out of the registers. He is four generations later. The pin was right and the reading of it here was wrong: this archive found *a* Grga at Ližnjan, decided it must be the one, and had to be corrected by the tree.

rows.lab: What would settle it
rows.text: The Ližnjan parish registers at the Državni arhiv u Pazinu, read as images rather than as an index — for Grga's own baptism about 1851, his death, and any emigration note in the margin. And Zagreb's Mirogoj burial records for Marija Defrančeski, 1884–1971, which would give a birthplace.

rows.lab: Corrected, 8 September 2026 — it is the wrong Monheim
rows.text: This page has been reading the pin's coordinates literally and searching **Bavaria**. That was a mistake, and a consequential one. Germany has two Monheims, and the one that matters is **Monheim am Rhein** in North Rhine-Westphalia — a Rhineland industrial town in the Kreis Mettmann, between Düsseldorf and Cologne, and the kind of place Yugoslav labour went to from the 1960s. Bavarian Monheim, in the Donau-Ries, is a market town of eight thousand people with no such history. **A pin dropped by autocomplete lands on the wrong one very easily.**

rows.lab: And with the right Monheim, the name is there
rows.text:
The German public telephone directory, searched nationally in every spelling, returns **exactly one private listing of «Defranceski» in the whole of Germany** — fused, no particle, spelt precisely as this family spells it. It is at **Langenfeld (Rheinland): five kilometres from Monheim am Rhein, in the same district, Kreis Mettmann.** (The only «Defranceschi» listing in Germany is a company at Mannheim — the German arm of the Italian winery-equipment firm, and nothing to do with anybody.)

They are living people, so this archive names no one. What it can say is this: **the pin is no longer sourceless.** A line drawn years ago from Ližnjan to Monheim, with no note and no date, turns out to point at the one corner of Germany where the surname is actually written the way this family writes it. That is not proof of a connection, and it is not being counted as one. It is the first thing that has ever supported the pin at all, and it converts a dead end into an address to ask at.

rows.lab: What would settle it
rows.text: Three routes, none of which this archive will take on its own. The **Croatian Catholic Mission** for Monheim–Langenfeld–Leverkusen keeps its own registers and would know when a family arrived. The **Kreis Mettmann Einwohnermeldeamt** holds registration records, restricted but obtainable by the family. And the simplest of all: the family at Langenfeld can be written to. That is David's to do, not this archive's.

why: Three things follow. The first is that a map pin with no source is worth chasing: Grga existed, and a whole household came back with him. The second is that this archive got the identification wrong — it found a Gregorius at Ližnjan and assumed he was the one, when the man on the pin was born eighty years later. That correction came from the family's own tree, not from the archive's cleverness, and it is left standing here rather than quietly rewritten. The third is unchanged: Monheim still carries no source of any kind, and stays unverified on this page in the same size type as everything else.

zagreb.heading: Zagreb: thirteen graves, and the parents cut into two of them
zagreb.lead: The city cemeteries of Zagreb publish a burial register — Mirogoj, Miroševac, Markovo polje and the rest — and it carries, for some burials, the names of the dead person's parents. Searched under every spelling in September 2026. It answers the map pin.

rows.lab: Milan and Dragutin, sons of Grgo and Marija
rows.text: **Milan Defrančeski**, died 24 May 2001, aged 78 — so born about 1923 — Mirogoj RKT 96A/II/61, parents entered as **«GRGO I MARIJA»**. And **Dragutin Defrančeski**, died 17 May 2004, aged 79 — born about 1925 — Mirogoj RKT 136/II/26, parents **«MARIJA I GRGA»**. Two brothers, in two graves, both naming the same father and mother. **This is the Grga of the pin, and he is now the father of two men whose graves can be visited.**

rows.lab: And it puts a date on him that the tree does not
rows.text: David's MyHeritage tree gives «Gregorius ‘Grgo’ Defranceski, born 1931 at Ližnjan, died at Zagreb». But a man whose sons were born in 1923 and 1925 was not born in 1931. Either the tree's year is wrong, or its Grgo is a third man of the name — a grandson, perhaps, named for him. Grga the father of Milan and Dragutin was born somewhere around 1890 to 1900. The archive is not going to pick a year; it is going to say that two independent records disagree and that the cemetery's is the one with a document behind it.

rows.lab: Marija, 1884–1971 — and the child in her grave
rows.text: **Marija Defrančeski**, died 3 June 1971, aged 87, so born about 1884: Mirogoj RKT 147A/II/58. In the same grave, **Zdenka Defrančeski, died 16 March 1945, aged two**, and not buried until 24 December 1971 — which means the child's remains were moved into her grave after Marija died. A little girl who died in March 1945, in the last weeks of the war, and waited twenty-six years to be laid with her.

rows.lab: Antun and Justina, in one grave
rows.text: **Antun Defrančeski**, died 5 June 1943 aged 67 — born about 1876 — and **Justina Defrančeski**, died 26 November 1963 aged 78 — born about 1885. Both Mirogoj RKT 136/II/43, and both buried on the same day, 28 November 1963: he was moved to lie with her when she died, twenty years after his own death. Justina is the name of Grga's daughter, baptised at Ližnjan on 4 October 1879 — nine years off, and this archive is not going to make them the same woman on a name.

rows.lab: An Uršula, at Miroševac
rows.text: **Uršula Defrančeski**, died 7 July 1963, aged 71, so born about 1892 — Miroševac RKT 240/I/45, sharing the grave with two men both called Josip, one dead 21 February 1976 aged 88 and the other 3 December 1979. Uršula is the name David's own great-grandmother carried. This is a different woman in a different city, and it is worth writing down that the name is in both branches.

rows.lab: And the rest of them
rows.text: **Blanka Defranceski**, born 16 December 1928, died 17 April 2019 aged 90, Markovo polje RKT 34/I/1610, parents **«ANĐELA I JOSIP»**. **Štefica Defrančeski**, born 7 December 1927, died 15 October 2016, parents «PAVAO I CECILIJA», buried in Milan's grave — so his wife. **Ana Defrančeski**, buried at Miroševac 3 May 1990, and a **Josip Defrancevski**, dead 29 April 1955 aged 48. Thirteen burials of the name in the city, spread over four cemeteries and eighty years.

zagreb.source_z: Gradska groblja Zagreb, «Tražilica pokojnika» — the city cemeteries' burial register, queried through its own OData service in September 2026 under Defrance*, Francesk* and Franceschi. Grave references are as the register gives them: cemetery, section, field, class, number. Parents' names appear only where the register carries them.

southistria.heading: Ližnjan is not a line. It is the tail of a southern-Istrian family that runs from 1667 to 2016.
southistria.lead: David keeps the unconnected households of the name in his own tree as **town nodes** — placeholder people called things like «Gologorica Defranceschi» or «Bakar Unknown Defranceschi», with the real individuals hung beneath them. There are eighteen of these. One of them is «PULA & Liznjan, Fasana, Istra, Medulin Defranceschi / Defranceski», and **Grgo of Ližnjan sits inside it**. Read out and followed through its citations, it is not a fourth family beside Carnia, Venice and Crete. It is one southern-Istrian family of thirty-one people with three hundred and fifty years of parish register behind it, and this archive had given it a page about a map pin.

rows.lab: How far back it goes
rows.text: **1667.** «Croatia, Church Books» has *Franceschina De Franceschi and Anto De Franceschi, 23 Oct 1667*, and another child of the same father on 8 November 1669. Then **Gaspero**, with children in 1688 and 3 April 1692. Then **Mattio**, whose son Antonio is entered in November 1704. That is four generations before the first date this site had for Ližnjan, and it is in the same registers this archive has been reading for Gračišće.

rows.lab: Where it actually lived
rows.text: Not Ližnjan. **Pula above all**, and **Fažana (Fasana)**, and **Premantura**, and **Medulin**, and **Barban** — the whole southern tip of the peninsula, Venetian territory, a different world from the Habsburg County of Pazin where our own family was. Baptisms and marriages at Pula in 1736, 1737, 1810, 1818, 1841, 1849, 1869; at Fažana in 1813, 1815, 1816, and a death there in 1846; at Premantura in 1809 and 1859. **Ližnjan is where the family was still living in 1931, not where it came from.**

rows.lab: Two outliers that matter
rows.text: A **Matto De Franceschi dead at ROVINJ on 27 December 1728**, and a **Bortolo** whose son Felice Antonio is baptised at **ŠTERNA** on 20 September 1778 — up in the Buje country, a hundred kilometres north. Southern Istria and the Bujština in one household file is either two families merged in the tree, or a family that moved twice.

rows.lab: And one that points at Friuli
rows.text: **Giambattista De Franceschi**, born before 1765, has two children entered at **ZOPPOLA in the province of Udine** — one in 1779 and one on 19 January 1811, the latter cited to «Italia, Udine, Stato Civile (Archivio di Stato)». Zoppola is in Friuli. **If that entry belongs in this cluster rather than being a Smart-Matched stranger, it points this family at Friuli and therefore at the Carnian direction, not the Cretan one.** It is the single most testable thing in the whole node, and it is testable: the Zoppola civil registers are filmed.

rows.lab: How it ends
rows.text: Three ways, and all three are the twentieth century happening to Istria. **Antonio Defranceschi, born 9 April 1894, died 11 February 1946 at Pula and buried in the k.u.k. Marinefriedhof** — the Austro-Hungarian naval cemetery, which by 1946 was a Yugoslav city's memory of an empire. **Grgo, born 1931 at Ližnjan, dead at Zagreb.** And two born at **Barban** who went to **France**: Marie, 22 February 1924 – 16 February 2002 at Charleville in the Moselle, and Ivan, 29 August 1931 – 16 September 2016 at **Cannes**. That is the *esodo*, and **France is a destination this archive's diaspora table did not have.**

rows.lab: What this changes here
rows.text: The Ližnjan page was written round a pin on a map and a note saying «Grga dies in Zagreb». Grga is real, and so is his family, and it is four times older and four times larger than this page assumed. **Ližnjan should stop being counted as a fourth family** and start being described as what the evidence shows: the last address of a southern-Istrian household that is in the Pula registers by 1667. Whether that household is Carnian, Cretan or neither is not yet settled — and the Zoppola entry is the thread to pull.

rows.lab: The Zoppola thread, pulled — and it snaps
rows.text:
This page said the Friulian entry was «the single most testable thing in the whole node». It has been tested, and **it is not evidence. It is a Smart Match.** Four things kill it.

**Two living Lucias.** The tree gives Giambattista a daughter **Lucia born 1779 and dead 1813**, and a second daughter **Lucia born 19 January 1811** — the second born while the first was alive. No Italian family names a second living daughter after her sister. These are two different men.

**The alias names a local family.** The 1813 citation reads «Giambattista De Franceschi **o Samassa**» — or Samassa, the Friulian plain's ordinary way of distinguishing branches. And **Samassa is a Zoppola surname in its own right**: Samassa Rachele and Samassa Giovanni are both in Zoppola's own civil registers. He is a Zoppola man of a Zoppola family.

**The surname is everywhere there.** A full-text sweep of the Friulian plain returns De Franceschi at **Azzano Decimo in 1897, Cordenons, Pordenone in 1888 and 1898, and Zoppola** — the commonest patronymic in Italy, behaving commonly.

**And even at best it was the wrong Friuli.** Zoppola is on the plain twenty-five kilometres west of Pordenone. **Carnia is sixty kilometres north, in the mountains.** A Zoppola link would not have been a Carnian link.

rows.lab: So where does that leave the cluster
rows.text: Where it was, and honestly. **Thirty-one people, in the Pula and Fažana registers from 1667, with no origin.** The one clue that pointed north was a graft, and removing it is worth more than keeping it would have been — the point of naming a testable thread is that it can fail. What remains testable is nearer home: the **outlier deaths at Rovinj in 1728 and the baptism at Šterna in 1778**, and Bertoša's study of Pula surnames from the confirmation lists of **1825**, which is exactly the place and period this household is thickest.

rows.lab: Corrected, September 2026 — the earliest entries are not Pula
rows.text: This page has carried «**Pula, 1667**» as the oldest record of the southern-Istrian family: Anto De Franceschi with children entered in October 1667 and November 1669. The index gives their place only as «Croazia, Austria», and the Pula reading was this archive's own. Resolved properly — index entry to image ark, image ark to film, film to catalogue — those baptisms are on **DGS 005497884, «Matična knjiga 1568–1917», the parish register of Svetvinčenat**. Forty kilometres north, a different parish, and a town whose De Franceschi are called **Carnian** by everyone who has studied them. The 1667 date stands. The place does not. The whole finding →

rows.lab: The marriage register, opened — and the first father and son of the name
rows.text:
**Everything above this row came from citations in a tree or from baptism indexes. This row comes from the marriage register itself**, which FamilySearch has never indexed and no one had opened: *Matična knjiga vjenčanih 1762–1815*, film 005497885.

Twenty-two of its openings have now been read line by line, and they put **six households of the name into the very years this page has always called a silence**:

- **9 February 1766** — *«Elena figlia di q. **Mattio de Franceschi**, nativa di questo Castello»* marries Mattio Sandalezza of Albona. Her father is dead, and is known from nothing else.
- **23 November 1771** — a witness entered as *«Jacobo **q. Jacobi de Franceschi**»*: a Giacomo whose father Giacomo was already dead.
- **10 June 1772** — that same man marries: *«**Giacobus filius Giacobi de Franceschi**, et Nicolina filia Nicolai Teserati»*. The first wedding of the name in the book.
- **25 January – 31 October 1773** — **Antonio de Franceschi** stands witness **six times**, usually beside Joannes Sain.
- **4 February 1773** — *«**Victorio de Franceschi filio Antonij**»*. **A father and a son of the name, named together, in one line.** It is the first such line this archive has for Svetvinčenat.
- **30 March 1773** — *«Maria **relicta q.m Gasparis de Franceschi**»* remarries under a Lenten dispensation. A Gasparo is dead, and his widow is in a hurry.

**What it changes.** The web is no longer nine households with a ninety-year hole in the middle; the hole has been entered, and it has people in it. **What it does not change** is the joining: not one of these six is merged with anyone already on the page. *(doc for every entry above; every identification is open.)*

rows.lab: ⭐⭐⭐ The whole Medulin presence of this surname is one woman, her parents and her children
rows.text:
**doc.** *Medulin deaths, 30 September 1896, entry 43* — read at native resolution, the word magnified until it could not be anything else:

> «**Fusca Kirac filia Petri et Mariae Defrancesco. agr: cath.**» — *ten months old, a lung complaint, buried the next day by Bylica.*

**The dead child is a Kirac. The Defranceschi is her mother** — ***Maria Defrancesco***, *wife of Petrus Kirac, labourer.* **The spelling is «Defrancesco», with an -o, and it is the only time that form has been seen in this parish.**

**⭐⭐ What makes it worth more than one entry is that it completes a shape.** *Three bearers of the name have now been found in the whole of the Medulin deaths book, 1801–1899, and* ***not one of them is a Medulin householder***:

- **1833** — *Mathæus Defranceschi q. Ant. fil.,* **miles** — *a soldier, dying where he was stationed*
- **1873** — *Maria,* **Ant. Verinic uxor** — *a Defranceschi daughter, married into a Verinic household*
- **1896** — *Maria* **Defrancesco**, *wife of Petrus Kirac — again a daughter, married into a Kirac household*

> **At Medulin the name arrives as a bride or a soldier. It never holds a house.**

***And that is exactly what the 1825 Pula confirmation lists already said from the other direction***: «De Franceschi» *stood at* **Premantura** *and* **Fažana**, *and* ***not at Medulin, Ližnjan or Šišan***. *Two independent sources, seventy years apart, agreeing that this village is where the name marries — not where it lives.*

⚠ **No join is claimed.** *Neither Maria is given a father, an age or a birthplace in her child's or husband's entry, and nothing here attaches either woman to a known household. They are two more women of the name in southern Istria, and the register that would name their fathers is the Medulin marriage book — forty-one frames, not yet opened.*

---

**⭐⭐⭐ LATER THE SAME DAY, THE MARRIAGE BOOK ANSWERED IT.** *Medulin marriages, 30 July 1874, entry 3:*

> «**Petrus Kirac** *Simonis fil. agr.*, Medulin house 143, aged 29 — **Maria Defranceschi** *q. Tommasi*, Medulin house 143, ***oriunda e Pomer***, aged 22»

***That is the same couple.*** *Twenty-two years later their daughter Fusca dies and the priest writes the mother's name as* «Defrancesco»; *here, at her wedding, it is written* «**Defranceschi**». **Same woman, two spellings, one parish.**

**And it gives the two things the death entry could not.** *Her father was* **Tommaso**, *already dead in 1874 — «q.» for* quondam. *And she was not a Medulin woman at all: she was* ***oriunda e Pomer***, *six kilometres round the bay, and had moved into her husband's house.*

**⭐⭐ So the pattern holds and gains a direction.** *The name still does not hold a house at Medulin — but we now know which way it came in from.* **Pomer.** *And Pomer is not new to this archive: it already held* **Pietro Defranceschi, born 1793**, *and Lucia Defranceschi — but every Pomer row was tree-only.* ***Maria and her father Tommaso are the first people of the name at Pomer that this archive holds on a register entry it has read with its own eyes.***

⚠ **No descent is claimed from Pietro b. 1793 to Tommaso.** *A shared village and a shared surname are not a join, and nothing in this entry names a grandfather.* **The book that would settle it is Pomer's own register, and Pomer is a separate parish this archive has not opened.**

**⭐⭐ And the facing page gives her mother.** *The right-hand page of the same opening carries the parents of both parties, and the row reads:* «*Simon Kirac* · *Catharina Lazarić vid.* · **def. Tomas De-franceschi** · **Magdalena Davić**».

> ***Tomas Defranceschi × Magdalena Davić, of Pomer — and their daughter Maria, born about 1852.***

**That is a whole household of the name, recovered from a single opening of a register nobody had read.** *And note the spelling:* «**De-franceschi**» *here, broken across the line;* «**Defranceschi**» *on the bride's own line four inches away;* «**Defrancesco**» *when her daughter dies in 1896.* ***Three forms, one parish, one family, twenty-two years.***

---

**⭐⭐ AND THE MARRIAGE BOOK, FINISHED, GIVES HER A SON.** *Medulin marriages, 21 September 1897:* **Lucas Kirac**, *aged 23,* «*filius Petri Kirac et* **Mariae Defrancesco**», *marries* **Fusca Demarin**, *daughter of Thoma Demarin and Maria Lorenzin.* ***Born about 1874 — the year his parents married.***

> **So the whole presence of this surname at Medulin, across three registers and two centuries, is ONE FAMILY.**
> *Maria Defranceschi of Pomer; her father Tomas and mother Magdalena Davić; her husband Petrus Kirac; her son Lucas, who grew up and married; her daughter Fusca, who died at ten months.* **And, quite separately, a soldier called Mathæus passing through in 1833.**

***That is what reading a parish end to end is for.*** *A surname search would have returned the 1833 soldier and stopped. Reading every entry of every opening — including the right-hand page, where only the PARENTS are named — turned one stray soldier into a household with a village, a generation above it and a generation below.*

⚠ **One near-miss, checked and rejected, recorded so nobody repeats it.** *On the register's last page a Kirac wife is written* «**Maria Perusco**». *At page scale the shape invites* «Defrancesco», *and a Kirac husband makes it tempting.* ***At native resolution it is plainly Perusco — a looped P, and no «Defrance» in it at all.*** *It is not a find.*

Every date above is from a citation in that tree, not from this archive's own reading of a register. The registers themselves are next. Added 21 September 2026: the Svetvinčenat marriage register 1762–1815 (FamilySearch film 005497885, images 6–27), read directly from the film — not from any tree or index.

smrtnilist.heading: ⭐⭐ A death certificate, sent by a Defranceschi — and it answers the question this page refused to answer
smrtnilist.lead: **David was sent a photograph of a** «**SMRTNI LIST**» — *a certified* «Prepis» *of a death entry, by a Defranceschi. It is the document [the Zagreb graves above](/liznjan/) have been asking for.*

rows.lab: What it says
rows.text:
«*U matici* **umrlih** *hrvatske* **Staro-katoličke župe sv. Križa u Zagrebu**, *svez.* **I**, *str.* **13**, *br.* **17**»

Died «**jedanaestoga novembra, Hiljadu devetstotina trideset i prve**» — **11 November 1931**.

«**Grga Defranceschi**, *bravar kod sekcije* **Držav. željeznica u Zagrebu**» — a **fitter with the State Railways** at Zagreb. Spouse: «**Marija rodj. Lovrencin, supruga mu**». Born: «**Ližnjan (Istra)**». Resident and died at «**Zagreb, Mošćenička ul. 12**». Religion: «**starokatolička**».

rows.lab: ⭐⭐ And it settles what this page said it would not settle
rows.text:
[The Zagreb section above](/liznjan/) says of the tree's «Gregorius ‘Grgo’ Defranceski, **born 1931** at Ližnjan, died at Zagreb»: *«a man whose sons were born in 1923 and 1925 was not born in 1931. Either the tree's year is wrong, or its Grgo is a third man of the name …* **The archive is not going to pick a year.**»

***It is the first. 1931 is the year he DIED.*** The tree carries his **death** year in a **birth** field — not a third man, a transposed column. **The refusal to guess was right, and the document rewards it.**

rows.lab: It is the same man, on four points
rows.text: The Mirogoj graves give Milan (d. 2001, b. ≈ 1923) and Dragutin (d. 2004, b. ≈ 1925) with parents «**GRGO I MARIJA**». The certificate gives a **Grga**, wife **Marija**, **born Ližnjan**, **died Zagreb**. *Wife, birthplace, city and the fit of the dates — a father dying in 1931 leaves sons of eight and six.* **⚠ Four agreements are not a proof**, and no register entry here names Milan or Dragutin as his children; the join is stated as an inference.

rows.lab: ⭐ It also fills an empty row
rows.text: «**Marija Lovrencin / Lorencin (Defranceschi)**» sat on the roster out of David's tree with **no dates, no place and no note at all**. She is now the named widow of a man with a date, a trade, a street and a parish. **⚠ And a further step is left untaken**: the same Zagreb section records a «**Marija Defrčeški, died 3 June 1971, aged 87**» at Mirogoj. *Widowed in 1931 at about forty-seven, dead at eighty-seven — it fits, and «Marija Defrančeški» is not a rare enough name to carry it. No dates are written onto her row.*

rows.lab: ⚠⚠ And he was not a Roman Catholic
rows.text: «**starokatolička**» — the **Croatian Old Catholic Church**, founded 1923, which kept its **own registers** outside the parish system this archive has walked for weeks. ***The word appears nowhere else in this archive.*** Any Defranceschi who joined it between 1923 and the 1940s is invisible to every search run here, and Zagreb was where the Istrian diaspora of those years was going. [Raised as its own row.](/worklist/)

rows.lab: ⚠ What the photograph does not show
rows.text:
The row beneath the birthplace — «**dan, mjesec i godina rodjenja**» — **is below the bottom edge of the frame**. His birth *date* is on the sheet and not in this archive. **A second photograph was taken and dropped in on 8 October — it is the plate below — and it has the same framing**, *so the row is still clipped. At the very bottom edge what may be an opening* «**17**» *is visible and nothing more;* ***it is not read here***. *One more photograph, aimed a few centimetres lower, would give the date and probably his parents.* [Raised.](/worklist/)

**And the form is a re-issue.** The printed «KRALJEVINA JUGOSLAVIJA … Banovina Savska» is overstamped «**Hrv. st. katolička Crkva · Nezavisna Država Hrvatska**», with «Za regulisanje penzije kod Financijske direkcije» across the head. ***So the copy was drawn under the NDH, 1941–45, for a pension claim on a death of 1931*** — the paper is evidence of two moments, ten years apart.

smrtnilist.source_s: Photograph of a «Smrtni list» (Prepis) in private hands, sent to David by a Defranceschi and read here on 8 October 2026; the file is kept in the project's `incoming/` folder. registers.heading: Fifty-one people, and what each of them actually rests on
registers.lead:
**Ližnjan has more people of the name than any Istrian parish except Svetvinčenat and Gologorica — and it has been searched less than almost any of them.** *Fifty-one people stand on this page's parish. Six mentions of Ližnjan exist across the whole of [the search log](/searched/), against a hundred and thirty-four for Svetvinčenat.*

*So before reading anything new, the archive asked a plainer question about what it already holds:* **for each of the fifty-one, what is the evidence?** *The answer separates them cleanly into three, and it is not flattering to the middle group.*

rows.lab: ⭐⭐ THE FIRST OF THE SEVENTEEN IS DONE — and the archive already had both halves of her life
rows.text:
**12 October 2026.** «Tusca Defranceschi, 1870–1870» *stood on the family tree and nothing else. Both her registers have now been read at the page.*

**Baptisms, page 15, Annus 1870, first entry** — «**9ⁿᵃ Januarii 1870**», **house 3**, «**Fusca, nata hodie**», *of* «**Matthæus Defranceschi**», ***agricola***, *and* «**Maria n. Primus**».

**Deaths, page 54** — «**mortua 6. Julii, sepult. 8 ejusdem**», **house 3, the same house**, «**Fusca filia Matthæi Defranceschi q. Matthæi et Mariæ n. Primus q. Paschalis**», «**6 mens.**», *of* «**debilitas**».

**Born 9 January, dead 6 July — five months and twenty-seven days**, *and the two books agree with each other on house and on parents without being asked.*

**⚠ And she was never called Tusca.** *The register reads* **Fusca** *in both entries. [A hand is only legible against itself](/method/), and the burial page hands over the comparison unasked: its* ***own first entry***, *same page and same hand, reads* «*Catharina filia di Giovanni Garbin e di* **Fosca**». *Fosca is a name this parish uses.* **Tusca is not a name.** *[Corrected](/corrections/) — though her id and her URL keep the old spelling, because [ids are frozen once minted](/method/) and a moved id is a dead link.*

**⚠ The part that should sting: this archive was already holding both halves and had not joined them.** *Its own* `register.json` *carried* «**Fusca · b. 9 Jan 1870**» *and* «**Tusca · d. 6 Jul 1870**» *as two separate leads with* ***identical parents***, *while the roster ignored both and copied the tree. The register did not tell us anything we could not have suspected from our own files — it told us we had not read them.*

**Sixteen of the seventeen to go**, *and fifty indexed Ližnjan records of the name are now harvested and tied to their books by ark, so the rest are located rather than hunted.*

rows.lab: ⭐⭐ TWO MORE — and the register says, in a single brace, that they were twins
rows.text:
**Anastasia and Maria** *both stood on the tree with nothing but* «1875–1875». *They are entries* **5 and 6 of 1875** *in the burial register — and the scribe wrote them as* ***one entry with a brace***, *the parents, the cause and the priest written once across both rows:*

> «**mortua die 22 Febr., sepulta die 23 ejusdem, 1875**» — **house 61** — *of* «**Gregorii Defranceschi**» *and* «**Mariæ Vojnić**», ***agr.***

**And both rows carry the same birth:** «**nat. 20/2 75**», *with an age of* «**dies 3**» *and a cause of* «**ordin.**» *against each.*

***Born on the same day, dead on the same day, buried on the same day, and bracketed together by the hand that wrote them: they were twins.*** *This archive had them as two unrelated children who happened to share a year.*

**⚠ The arithmetic is left as the register wrote it** — *born the 20th and dead the 22nd is two days, and the scribe put* «dies 3» *against each. He may have counted inclusively, or counted to the burial. It is recorded rather than quietly fixed to fit.*

rows.lab: ⭐⭐ A FOURTH — and the Ližnjan baptism book turns out to carry death margins AND anagrafe references
rows.text:
«Justina», *carrying* «1879–1952» *from the tree, is* **page 56, entry 22 of 1879, house 61** — *and her name in the book is* «**Magdalena Justina**», *born* **3 October 1879**, «hora circ. 3 pomer.», *to* «**Gregorius Defranceschi**» *and* «**Maria Vojnić**». ***She is the twins' sister***, *same house, same parents.*

**⭐ Beside her baptism, in Croatian and a later hand:**

> «**Umrla u Ližnjanu dana 18. V. 1952** (mat. knj. umrlih str. 36 d. 2/52 Ližnjan.)»

*The bare* «1952» *is now* **18 May 1952**, *and the margin cites the death register's own page and entry number. [This is exactly what the Gologorica margins do](/gologorica-line/) — a baptism book standing in for a register nobody here can reach.*

**⭐ And a second thing the page gives away: a column of** «**Anagr. p. 305 III.7**» *references, one against every entry —* ***page and family number in a Status Animarum***. **Ližnjan has an anagrafe, and its baptism register indexes it entry by entry.** *Neither the book nor the index was known here.*

rows.lab: ⚠⚠ AND ONE OF THE SEVENTEEN WAS NEVER A SEVENTEENTH — the archive already had him
rows.text:
«Mattheus Defranceschi, 1891–1891» *stood on the tree with no document.* **He is page 108, entry 7 of 1891, house 3:**

> «**mort. 18 Febr., sepul. 19 ejusdem, 1891**» — «**Mathæus Defranceschi, Mathæi et Annæ Skoko**» — «**nat. 25/1 90**».

***Born 25 January 1890, dead 18 February 1891*** — *and this archive* **already held him**, *as* «Mathæus Defranceschi, 1890–1891», *from the burial index, with the right year. Two rows, one child. [Corrected](/corrections/); nothing deleted, because [ids are frozen](/method/) and the join is written on both.*

**⚠ And it is not one row. Comparing all thirteen remaining tree-only Ližnjan people against the register-sourced ones of the same name and neighbouring years turns up FOUR pairs that look like the same child entered twice** — *once from a document, once from the tree, a year or a spelling apart:*

| tree-only row | record-sourced row | |
|---|---|---|
| Mattheus b. **1891** d. 1891 | Mathæus b. **1890** d. 1891 | **✔ PROVED one child, 12 Oct** |
| Josephus b. **1886** d. 1888 | Josephus b. **1887** d. 1888 | *probable — unread* |
| Mattheus b. **1858** | Mathæus b. **1857** | *probable — unread* |
| Antonio b. **1848** | Antonio b. **1846** | *weaker — unread* |

**Only the first has been read on the page. The other three are recorded as SUSPECTED and nothing has been merged**, *because a year's difference between a tree and an index is exactly what a register exists to settle, and guessing would put the archive back where the tree left it.*

rows.lab: ⭐⭐ THE ANAGRAFE, NOT THE HOUSE NUMBER, IS WHAT HOLDS A LIŽNJAN FAMILY TOGETHER
rows.text:
**Page 99, entry 7 of 1888** — *and the scribe wrote the name in the left margin as well as in the column:*

> «**Josephus Defranceschi**» · «**Mort. — Martii, Sep. — ejusdem, 1888**» · **house 82** · **Anagr. p. 305, III. 9** · «**Josephus Defranceschi, Gregorii et Maria Vojnić**» · «**an. 1, mens. 11**» · «**nat. 15/4 86**»

**Born 15 April 1886, dead in March 1888 at a year and eleven months** — *the age and the birth agree with each other, and the day/month/year form of* «15/4 86» *is the one this book uses throughout* («nat. 2/5 851» *against an age of* «ann. 23, m. 8, d. 26»).

**⚠ THE DEATH DAY IS BLANK IN THE REGISTER ITSELF.** *The scribe wrote* «Mort. — Martii» *and* «Sep. — ejusdem» *and never filled the days in. That is the book's gap, not a failure of reading, and no day is invented here.*

**⚠⚠ TWO ROWS, ONE CHILD — and this time the TREE was right and the INDEX was wrong.** *This archive held* `josephus-defranceschi-1887` *from the index* («b. Mar 1887») *and* `josephus-defranceschi-1886` *from the family tree* («1886»). ***The register says 15 April 1886.*** **The tree had it; the index did not.** *That is the exact reverse of [the Mathæus duplicate settled the same week](/corrections/), where the index was right and the tree a year out — and it is a useful corrective to assuming an index outranks a tree.*

**⭐ And the anagrafe reference ties the household together ACROSS A MOVE.** *This entry cites* **Anagr. p. 305, III. 9**; *[Magdalena Justina's baptism](/who/justina-defranceschi/) cites* **p. 305, III. 7** — *same page, same family, different person number —* ***though she was entered at house 61 in 1879 and he at house 82 in 1888***. *The house number moves; the anagrafe family does not. [That makes the anagrafe the better key for this parish than the house number](/liznjan/).*

**The household of Gregorius Defranceschi and Maria Vojnić now stands at four children buried small:** *the twins Maria and Anastasia (20–22 February 1875), a Maria of 1878 still unread, Magdalena Justina (1879–1952, who lived), and this Josephus.*

rows.lab: NINE stand on a page of the register itself
rows.text: *Nine carry an* **image ark** — *a reference to a photographed page, not to somebody's index card. As of 11 October each of those arks has been traced to the volume it is physically bound into, by listing every ark in every Ližnjan book and finding ours inside:* **Births (Rođeni) 1816–1883** (`9R2Z-44D`), **Marriages (Vjenčani) 1815–1902** (`9R2Z-44C`) *and* **Deaths (Umrli) 1815–1900** (`9R2Z-4WG`). *These nine are as solid as this archive gets: Maria Schiffic b. 1817, Matteo b. 1835, Cattarina b. 1844, Mattio b. and d. 1850, Joannes b. 1875, Anastasia b. 1876, Maria b. 1882, and Maria Marcorich and Lucia Sandalj by marriage.*

rows.lab: TWENTY-ONE stand on an index entry
rows.text: *Twenty-one carry a* **persona ark** — *FamilySearch's index of a record, which is a transcription made by somebody else from a page this archive has never seen. An index is a finding aid, not a document.* **It is good evidence that a record exists and poor evidence of what the record says** — *every wrong parent, wrong year and wrong spelling this archive has corrected came through one.*

rows.lab: ⚠ SEVENTEEN stand on a family tree and nothing else
rows.text: *Seventeen have* **no ark of any kind**, *and their source is* `myheritage` — *the live family tree. They may be perfectly right. Nothing has ever been checked against a register.* **That is a third of Ližnjan's people resting on a copy of a copy**, *and it is recorded here rather than left to look like documented fact.*

rows.lab: ⭐ And fifteen of those seventeen are REACHABLE — the exact entries, named
rows.text:
*This is the part worth acting on. The three Ližnjan volumes are now pinned, so their year ranges can be set against the seventeen:*

**THIRTEEN have a birth year inside Births 1816–1883** — *Mathaei 1821, Madalena 1827, Antonio 1848, Guiffina 1851, Mattheus 1858, Paschalis 1863, Fusca 1870, Ana 1873, Anastasia 1875, Maria 1875, Antonius-Mario 1876, Justina 1879, Maria 1883.*

**EIGHT have a death year inside Deaths 1815–1900** — *Madalena 1828, Fusca 1870, Paschalis 1873, Anastasia 1875, Maria 1875, Maria 1884, Josephus 1888, Mattheus 1891.*

⭐ *And the death register reaches two the birth register cannot:* **Josephus, born 1886, and Mattheus, born 1891, both fall after the birth book closes in 1883** — *but both died inside the death book. Where a child is unreachable at one end of its life it may be reachable at the other.*

*Only* **two** *of the seventeen cannot be reached at all:* **Catarina Kisdaris and Josephi** — *and both are bare parent-names carrying no date whatever, so there is nothing to look up.*

rows.lab: ⚠ What has NOT been done, so the list above is not mistaken for work
rows.text:
**No Ližnjan register page has been read for this.** *The volumes were identified, not opened. FamilySearch serves its images only to a signed-in account, and* [this archive does not enter credentials](/method/) — *David signs in and a session drives. The waypoint work above needed no login because the volume tree is public while the images are not.*

*So what stands here is* **a reading list with every entry's book and year range established**, *not a set of findings. The distinction is the whole method.*

rows.lab: ⚠⚠ AND THE REAL LESSON OF LIŽNJAN: this archive kept finding things it already had
rows.text:
**⭐⭐ The pattern behind all of this week's Ližnjan work, now counted.**

*Three separate times in two days, a Ližnjan person turned out to be sitting in this archive's own* `register.json` *as an* ***indexed lead nobody ever took up***, *while the roster carried the tree's version of the same person — or nothing at all:*

1. **[Fusca, 1870](/who/tusca-defranceschi/)** — *both halves of her life held as two leads, parents identical, never joined; the roster took the tree and the wrong spelling.*
2. **[Mathæus, 1890–1891](/who/math-us-defranceschi/)** — *held from the burial index with the right year, and duplicated by the tree with the wrong one.*
3. **[Fusca née Lazarić, d. 1888](/who/fusca-defranceschi-lazaric/)** — *a* **wife of the name**, *held as lead* `XQM3-P992` *and* ***never in the roster in any form***.

**So the files were counted.** `register.json` *holds* **24** *leads placed at Ližnjan.* **15 of them are cited by no roster row at all.**

*Three of those fifteen are people documented from the page this week — Fusca 1870 and the twins Maria and Anastasia of 1875 — whose roster rows now cite the* ***register image*** *rather than the index lead, so the lead still reads as unused. That is a bookkeeping artefact and is said so here rather than counted as a gap.*

**The rest are genuinely untaken**, *and most are children of Defranceschi daughters who married out — Ruman, Perković, Jelčić, Našković — plus* «Mattio Franceschi, 1799 – 20 Dec 1839» *and* «Giovanni Defranceschi, 1845 – 11 Nov 1846», *who are of the name outright.*

**⚠ The lesson is not that the index is good.** *It is that* ***this archive kept finding things it already had***. *The register settles what the index garbles —* «Antonii Defranceschi Or Lazarić» *is a flattened parent list that the page resolves instantly into* «**uxor Antonii Defranceschi nata Lazarić**» — *but the lead was the thing that should have sent somebody to the page years ago.*

**The newest of the three was read on 12 October:** *page 101, entry 23 of 1888, house 75 —* «**Mort. 17 Augusti, Sep. 19 ejusdem, 1888** — Fusca uxor Antonii Defranceschi nata Lazarić». *[She is in the roster now](/who/fusca-defranceschi-lazaric/),* **without a birth year**, *because the index's* «1821» *can only come from an age this session did not reach, and an index is not a document.*

rows.lab: ⭐ A DAUGHTER WHO MARRIED OUT, AND SEVEN CHILDREN NOBODY HERE HAD
rows.text:
**But the opening gave something it was not asked for.** *Page 69, second entry,* `Parentes`:

> *Pater* «**Antonio Nascovich fu Giovanni**» · *Mater* «**Maddalena Defranceschi fu Matteo**»

***A Defranceschi daughter married out, and a Matteo already dead by 1857.*** *She is* **not** *[the Maddalena this archive holds](/who/maddalena-defranceschi/), who died in 1849. [She is in the roster now](/who/maddalena-defranceschi-naskovic/).*

**⭐ And she had a household of seven.** *The harvested index carries* **seven** *Našković children to a* «Maddalena Defranceschi» *at Ližnjan — Euffemia 1852, Cattarina 1855, Cattarina 1856, Cattarina 1857, Antonius 1859, Joannes 1869, Josephus 1873 —* ***three daughters given the same name, which usually means the first two died***. **None of the seven is in this roster and none has been read.** *Leads, not people.*

**⚠ Her father is not asserted.** *The entry says* «fu Matteo». *This archive's* `register.json` *holds lead* `XQM3-21M6` — «**Mattio Francesch, b. 1799, d. 20 December 1839**» — *which fits, and which* **no roster row has ever taken up**. ***A date that fits is not a match***, *so it is named as a candidate and left there.*

**⚠ WHAT WAS LOOKED FOR AND NOT FOUND — the exact terms, because [a nil that names no terms is an assertion about a list nobody kept](/method/).**

*The target was the* **Mattheus 1858 / Mathæus 1857 pair** — *the roster holds both, one from the tree and one from the index, and the register was to settle whether they are one child.*

*The index record that put a Defranceschi birth on this frame is* «**Matteo Defraceschi · Maria Primus**», 1857. **Both pages of the opening were read down the** `Parentes` **columns, every entry** — *page 68 and page 69, about eighteen entries.* ***No birth to a Defranceschi father and a Primus mother is on this opening.*** *The fathers on page 68 are Fedel, Giuseppe, Bucovich, Millasevich, Costip…, Bolsun, Carmin; on page 69, Voinich, Nascovich, Clinich, Mocorich, Baldessi, Legovich, Sebetich, Millosevich.*

**So the pair is NOT settled**, *and the 1857 Defranceschi birth is somewhere other than where the frame number put it — most likely the facing frames 31 or 33, which were not opened.*

rows.lab: ⭐⭐ A THIRD CHILD IN 1875 — and an entry that names a mother and no father
rows.text:
**Page 68, entry 10 of 1875**, **house 71**, *Anagr.* **II. 2**:

> «**Mortuus die 19 Sept., Sepult. 21 ejusdem, 1875**» · «**Joannes fil. Justinæ Defranceschi**» · «**dies 22**» · «**nat. 28/8 75**» · «**ordinaria**» · *D. G. Smak, parochus*

***Born 28 August 1875, dead 19 September, buried the 21st, aged twenty-two days*** — *and the arithmetic agrees with the register's own figure for once, which it did not for [the twins](/liznjan/).*

**⚠ THE ENTRY NAMES HIS MOTHER AND NO FATHER.** *Every other entry on the opening names both:* «filia Antonii et Antoniæ Fedel», «filia Joannis et Luciæ Perković nata Josephi Klunić», «filia Antonii et Annæ Fedel». ***That contrast is what the register says, and nothing beyond it is asserted.*** *This parish's death register carries no legitimacy column — the baptism register does — so the shape of the entry is the only evidence there is.*

**⚠ A SECOND JUSTINA.** *His mother is* **not** *[Magdalena Justina](/who/justina-defranceschi/), who was born in 1879, four years after this child died. Another Justina Defranceschi stood at Ližnjan in 1875 and this archive holds no record of her at all.*

**He is the third child of the name buried at Ližnjan in 1875.** *[The twins](/who/maria-defranceschi/) went together on 22 February; he followed in September. Three of the parish's Defranceschi children in one year.*

**And he clears a flagged lead.** *[The gate's new](/worklist/)* `check-leads` *had him as one of six people the roster already held with an unlinked lead* (`XQM3-118S`). *Linked, and read. The count falls* **6 → 5**.

rows.lab: ⚠ THE DEATH REGISTER SCOUT — eleven of the name, but the sweep was NOT end to end and says so now
rows.text:
**⚠⚠ READ THE CORRECTION FIRST.** *This section was written claiming the death register had been covered* ***end to end***. *It had not: the crop read about the* **top 44% of every page**. *[The full account is on /corrections/](/corrections/). The eleven people listed below are real and were read on the page; what is withdrawn is the claim of completeness. The book is being re-scanned.*

---

**⭐⭐⭐ THE WHOLE BOOK, FRAME BY FRAME — 72 frames, 1815 to 1900, every opening looked at.**

*Not a transcription: the* `NOMEN DEFUNCTI` *column of* ***both pages of every opening*** *was rendered at native resolution and read for the surname, with every doubtful word magnified. [That is a scout, not a walk](/method/), and the row says* `walked:false` *for that reason.*

**ELEVEN people OF THE NAME are buried in this book.** *Four were already documented here this week; two are new; one is still unverified.*

| frame | date | house | the entry |
|---|---|---|---|
| 17 | **6 Jan 1849** | 17 | «Maddalena fu Matteo Defranceschi» |
| 18 | **16 Jan 1850** | 17 | «Matteo figlio di Matteo Defranceschi» |
| 26 | *1861* | — | «Gregorius Defranceschi…» — **⚠ not yet verified** |
| 31 | 6 Jul 1870 | 3 | «Fusca filia Mathæi Defranceschi» · *[read](/who/tusca-defranceschi/)* |
| 37 | 22 Feb 1875 | 61 | the twins **Maria** and **Anastasia** · *[read](/who/maria-defranceschi/)* |
| 38 | 19 Sep 1875 | 71 | «Joannes fil. Justinæ Defranceschi» · *[read](/who/joannes-defranceschi/)* |
| 49 | **11 Oct 1884** | 82 | «**Maria Defranceschi**» · ***closes one of the seventeen*** |
| 53 | Mar 1888 | 82 | «Josephus Defranceschi, Gregorii et Maria Vojnić» · *[read](/who/josephus-defranceschi/)* |
| 54 | 17 Aug 1888 | 75 | «Fusca uxor Antonii Defranceschi nata Lazarić» · *[read](/who/fusca-defranceschi-lazaric/)* |
| 58 | 18 Feb 1891 | 3 | «Mathæus Defranceschi, Mathæi et Annæ Skoko» · *[read](/who/math-us-defranceschi/)* |
| 64 | **21 Dec 1896** | 3 | «**Josephus Defranceski, Matthæi servi**» · ***new*** |

**⭐ SEVEN MORE are children of Defranceschi DAUGHTERS who married out** — *the surname is in the mother's place, which is why no search for the name as a principal would ever have found them:*

| frame | year | the entry |
|---|---|---|
| 33 | 1872 | Mathæus **Ruman**, *Josephi et Mariæ Defranceschi* |
| 35 | 1873 | a child of *Antonii et Magdalenæ Defranceschi* — **Našković** |
| 35 | 1873 | Joannes Baptista, *Josephi et Catharinæ Defranceschi* — **Jelčić** |
| 41 | ~1879 | Gregorius **Sandalj**, *Joannis et Luciæ* |
| 42 | 1880 | Magdalena **Ruman**, *Josephi et Mariæ Defranceschi* |
| 46 | 1883 | Josephus **Ruman**, *Josephi et Mariæ Defranceschi* |
| 50 | 1885 | Josephus, *Josephi et Catharinæ de Franceschi* — **Jelčić** |

**⚠ None of those seven is in this roster.** *They are recorded here as what they are — entries read on a page, not people minted — because each needs its own reading before it becomes a record.*

**⭐⭐ AND THE LAST ENTRY OF THE NAME IN THE BOOK CHANGES THE SPELLING.** *21 December 1896, house 3:* «**Josephus Defranceski, Matthæi servi**», *twenty months old, dead of* «angina». ***The -ski ending the family uses today, written in the register in 1896*** — *every earlier entry in this book spells it* «Defranceschi». *And his father is a* **servus**, *where [the Matthæus of the same house 3 was an* ***agricola*** *in 1870](/who/tusca-defranceschi/). [He is minted](/who/josephus-defranceski/).*

**What the scout also establishes, which a hit list cannot:**

- **The register's content runs frames 3–66.** *Frame 0 is the HDA title card, 1 a resolution target, 2 the marbled cover with its label* «Ližnjan — Mat. knjiga umrlih od 1815 do 1900 god.»; *67 is* «END OF ITEM», *68* «KRAJ» *and reel 23, 69–71 targets.*
- **Two frames are RE-SHOOTS with loose documents laid across the page.** *Frame* **16** *repeats frame 15 with a German* «**Tauf-Schein**» — *Diözese Seckau, Steiermark, a baptismal certificate of* **1916** — *lying on it; frame* **60** *repeats 59 with a* «**Certificato d'ispezione cadaverica**». *[The same thing the Gologorica reels do](/gologorica-line/), and it means* ***72 frames is not 72 openings***.
- **The book carries ANAGRAFE references** — «p. 325 III.5», «II. 85» — *against its entries from about 1870, [just as the baptism book does](/liznjan/).*
- *Frame 29's right page carries a long Italian narrative entry of several lines, unlike anything around it. It was not read.*

**⚠ WHAT THIS SCOUT DOES NOT CLAIM.** *It read the* `NOMEN DEFUNCTI` *column. It did* **not** *read the Morbus, Ætas or Anagrafe columns of entries that carry no Defranceschi, and it did not transcribe a single year end to end. A woman of the name entered only by her husband's surname, with no* «nata», *would not be caught by it. One candidate — frame 26, 1861 — remains unverified.*

rows.lab: ⭐⭐⭐ WHERE THEY CAME FROM — the first Defranceschi at Ližnjan, 1815, and the word that nearly said it
rows.text:
**⭐⭐⭐ THE EARLIEST DEFRANCESCHI EVENT IN ANY LIŽNJAN BOOK — the marriage that starts the parish's line.**

**Ližnjan** «Liber Copulatorum», **page 1, entry 2**, *the second marriage the book ever records:*

> «**12 Novembre 1815**» · **house 17** · *SPONSUS* «**Mario de Franceschi deto Marulin di Antonio**», *catolico, Ætas* **21**, *celibes* · *SPONSA* «**Maddalena Percouich di Antonio**», *catolica, Ætas* **27**, *celibes* · *TESTES* «Giacomo Bubich di Iseppo», «Antonio Clunich di Stefano», «Gregorio Iucopila»

**Aged twenty-one in November 1815, so born about 1794. His father is Antonio.** *And this is the couple whose children fill house 17 in the baptism book — Antonio 1819, Mattia 1821, Gregorio 1822 — all to* «Mattio Franceschi di Antonio» *and* «Mandalena Pecouichi».

**⭐ HE CARRIES A BYNAME:** «**deto Marulin**» — *detto Marulin, «called Marulin».*

**⚠ And the byname was nearly read as a PLACE.** *The same book, sixteen years later, writes a groom as* «**Giacomo Micalouich figlio di Giorgio della Carniola di Madolin**» — *Carniola, and Madolin for Medulin, the next parish. Against that,* «ma—rulin» *looked like it might be* «Madolin», *which would have made it an origin rather than a nickname.* **[It is not](/method/):** *at nine times magnification the letter has no ascender, and this scribe gives every* **d** *a tall one —* «di Antonio», «de Franceschi», «deto» *itself, all on the same line. It is an* **r**. *The hand decided it, not the plausibility.*

**⚠ NO PLACE OF ORIGIN IS GIVEN, and that is worth stating carefully.** *The book does record origins when it wants to —* «della Carniola di Madolin» *proves it —* ***but that entry is from 1831, in a later and far more verbose format***. *The 1815 page is terse: four columns, no* `Conditio` *for the spouses, no parents named. **So the silence here is weak evidence at best, and no conclusion is drawn from it.** [A nil names the terms tried](/method/): what was looked for was a* «di» *or* «della» *phrase in the Nomen cell, and there is none beyond the patronymic.*

**⭐ A second marriage, and a daughter going out.** *Page 15, entry 113:* «**23 Febbrajo 1848**», *house 41 —* «**Martino Mocovich**» *and* «**Maria figlia Matteo Defranceschi**», *with* «**Defranceschi**» *written again in the* `Genitori della sposa` *column. A daughter of a Matteo, marrying out in 1848.*

rows.lab: ⭐⭐⭐ THE 1815 GROOM'S OWN BURIAL — and «Marulin» written on him a second time
rows.text:
**Ližnjan** «Liber Defunctorum», **page 93**:

> «**Addì 20 Xbre 1839**» · **house 17** · «**Mattio Franceschi d.to Marulin, agr.**» · «**ann. 40**»

***He married into house 17 in 1815 and died in it in 1839.*** *Antonio was born there in 1819, Mattia in 1821, Gregorio in 1822.*

**⭐ The byname is on him twice.** *The marriage called him* «**Mario de Franceschi deto Marulin di Antonio**»; *the burial calls him* «**Mattio Franceschi d.to Marulin**» — *different book, different hand, twenty-four years apart.* **That closes the reading that nearly made «Marulin» into «Madolin»**, *i.e. Medulin: a place does not follow a man to his grave as a* «detto».

**⚠ His age does not agree with itself.** *1815 says* **21**; *1839 says* **40**. *Born about 1794 or about 1799 — five years apart, both the parish's own figures, neither corrected here.*

**⚠ And this archive had the lead all along.** `register.json` *held* `XQM3-21M6` — «**Mattio Francesch, b. 1799, d. 20 Dec 1839**» — *cited by no roster row. It was named as a candidate yesterday and left unproved. It is read now.*

rows.lab: ⭐⭐⭐ «NATA E MEDOLINO» — the one plain statement of origin the books have given
rows.text:
**Ližnjan** «Liber Copulatorum», **page 22, entry 168**:

> «**1 Junii 1861**» · **house 59** · «**Antonius Defranceski q. Matthæi, agr.**», *Ætas* **41**, ***Viduus*** · «**Fosca nata Lazarić q. Simeonis, V[idu]a q. Antonii Mohorić agr., nata e Medolino**»

**[Fusca née Lazarić](/who/fusca-defranceschi-lazaric/) was born at MEDULIN** — *Medolino is the Italian name for it, five kilometres down the cape.* [Her burial of 1888](/who/fusca-defranceschi-lazaric/) *gave* «nat. 30/4 1821» *and an age of 67; this gives the place to go with the date.*

**⭐ Both were widowed** — *he* «Viduus», *she* «vidua q. Antonii Mohorić». ***Before 1861 she was a Mohorić***, *which is why she appears in no earlier Defranceschi entry.*

**⭐ And he is the 1815 groom's son.** «*Antonius Defranceski* **q. Matthæi**», *forty-one in June 1861, so born about 1820 — and the baptism book has an* **Antonio born 15 September 1819** *at house 17 to the couple of the 1815 marriage. Age and patronymic both fit;* **no single entry says so**, *so it is recorded as a chain and not as proof.*

**⚠ And Medulin is now the open question.** *[The lines diagram carries it](/lines/) as a household not yet placed: the only two people this roster puts at Medulin are* **tree-only** — *a Mattheus b. 1793 and an Antonio b. 1819, which are the Ližnjan founders' own dates.* ***Ližnjan's books begin in 1815 and cannot say where the first Defranceschi came from.*** *Medulin's marriages run* **1666–1704** *and have never been opened.*

medulin.heading: The archive knew two of her children. The Medulin baptism book gives eight.
medulin.lead: **Maria Defranceschi — «oriunda e Pomer», daughter of the late Tomas Defranceschi and Magdalena Davić — married Petrus Kirac at Medulin on 30 July 1874.** *This archive met her twice by accident: once as a name in her daughter Fusca's death entry in 1896, spelled «Defrancesco», and once in the marriage register that named her father. Two children were documented, both of them met sideways.* ***Reading the Medulin baptism book end to end turns her into a mother of eight, across fourteen years, in two houses — and the children's own margins carry them forward to Pula in 1966 and to Ližnjan in 1964.***

rows.lab: 1874 · Lucas
rows.text: **Born and baptised 16 August 1874**, entry 16, page 103. *The roster had him as «about 1874», inferred backwards from his age at his 1897 marriage.* **It is now a date**, and the same entry carries a death cross — ✝ **16 September 1930**. *The reading was settled against the scribe's own hand: he writes* **16** *in the baptism-day column and* **«natus 16 aug.»* *in the next, the same glyph twice in one row.*

rows.lab: 1876 · Stephanus
rows.text: **Born 23 December 1876, baptised the 24th**, house 142, entry 48, page 109. *Godparents Lucas Lazarić and his wife Anna.* **The margin is in Croatian and modern:** «*Umro u Puli dana 27·X·1966*», *entered by the Pula registrar.* ***He lived ninety years and died in the city.*** *Not previously known to this archive.*

rows.lab: 1879 · Catharina
rows.text: **Born 18 February 1879, baptised the 19th**, entry 9, page 113, **house 143** — *the same house the marriage register gave for her parents in 1874.* *Godparents Lucas Lazarić with Anna his wife, the same couple as 1876.* *Not previously known.*

rows.lab: 1882 · Maria
rows.text: **Born 13 March 1882, baptised the 20th**, entry 14, page 122, **house 174** — *the family has moved.* *Godfather Lucas Lazarić again.* *Not previously known.*

rows.lab: 1884 · Thomas, who lived six days
rows.text: **Born 7 August 1884, baptised the 8th**, entry 35, page 131, house 176; *the father is written out in full here —* «**Petrus Kirac Simonis fil.**», *matching the «son of Simon» of the marriage entry.* **«obiit 13 august 1884».** ***He was named for his mother's dead father, Tomas Defranceschi of Pomer, and he did not live a week.***

rows.lab: 1885 · Agnes, who married and went to Ližnjan
rows.text: **Born 8 August 1885**, entry 27, page 133. *The margin records her marriage —* «*coniugata 30/5 1906 cum Antonio Fedel*» — *and then, in a 1960s registrar's hand, her death.* **The place name in that margin is «Ližnjanu».** ***A daughter of this Pomer Defranceschi married out of Medulin and died in the very parish this archive has been reading from the other end.***

rows.lab: 1888 · Antonius, who lived nine months
rows.text: **Born 25 January 1888, baptised the 27th**, entry 3, page 140 — *the surname spelled* «**Chirac**» *by this scribe.* *Godparents* «*Petrus Chirac cum Agatha uxore*». **«obiit 4 Novembris 1888».** *Not previously known.*

rows.lab: 1895 · Fusca
rows.text: *Already held by this archive, and the only one of the eight it had by name:* **died at Medulin 30 September 1896, aged ten months**, *of a lung complaint.* ***Her death entry is where the archive first met her mother*** — *and it is the reason this book was opened at all.*

rows.lab: ⚠ And a ninth that cannot be claimed
rows.text: **December 1889, page 145: an infant «Petrus Kirac», whose mother's cell reads «Maria … Defrancesco» and whose godparents are «Petrus Kirac et Agatha uxor ejusdem» — the identical couple who stood for Antonius in 1888.** *Everything points one way.* ***But the father's cell is EMPTY.*** *Not faded —* **empty**: *a contrast stretch of that cell at seven times magnification returns clean ruled lines and no ink at all.* *A blank* **Genitores Patris** *in this book means something, and until it is established what, this child is recorded as* **an unconstrued entry naming the surname**, *not as a ninth child.* **The nil here is about the father, not about the name.**

decrees.heading: One parish book, three states, and a surname changed twice in one lifetime
decrees.lead: **A one-name study is a study of spellings, and this register shows who was doing the spelling.** *The Medulin baptism book's margins are thick with official surname changes, and they run in both directions under three sovereigns. None of them touch a Defranceschi — the name is not a Medulin name — but they are the machinery that produced the nine spellings this archive does carry, and they are dated, numbered and citable.*

rows.lab: Austria · the 1880s
rows.text: *A footnote at page 121:* «**Decreto I.R. Luogotenenza Tergestina** … *concessa est immutatio quoad modum scribendi* … **Tomasich in Tomasić**». ***The Imperial-Royal Lieutenancy at Trieste, granting a change in the manner of writing a name.*** *Permission, applied for and given.*

**Dozens of marginal notes, each citing a «decreto del Prefetto di Pola» with its date and number.** *Collected while reading: Radossevich → **Ardossi** (13.1.1931 NR 286; 17.1.1931 NR 295), Grahalich → **Gracali** (18.9.1930), Leverić → **Leveri** (29.10.1930), Mihalevich → **Micali**, Giacopila → **Michelini**, Lazarić → **Lazzari** (1933), Rakić → **Racchi**, Privrat → **Privato** (1931), Sirovich → **Sironi** (28.5.1938 NS 714), Vojak → **Vogliacco** (20.X.1935; 22.X.1937 MV/237; 22.III.1933).* ***Not requests. Decrees.***

rows.lab: Yugoslavia · 1961–1975
rows.text: *Typed slips pasted into the book, each citing* «**čl. 29 Zakona o ličnim imenima**» — *article 29 of the Law on Personal Names — and signed by the* **matičar** *at Pula.* *Seen: **Vogliacco Pietro → Vojak Petar** (26·VII·1961), **Vogliacco Fosca → Vojak Fosca** (22·VI·1965), **Lazzari Antonio → Lazarić Antun** (26·VII·1961), **Riccato Lucia → Rikato Lucia** (1961).* ***Every one of them undoing a decree of the 1930s, name for name.***

rows.lab: ⭐ And one man whose name was changed twice, by two states
rows.text: **Petrus Vojak, baptised at Medulin 27 June 1871, entry 18, page 95.** *On his own entry the Prefect of Pola's decree of* **22·X·1937** *makes him* **Vogliacco**. ***Glued over that same entry*** *is the 1961 slip restoring him to* **Vojak Petar**. *He was born under Austria, renamed under Italy, and renamed back under Yugoslavia —* **and the page carries all three, one on top of the other.**
